sarah.ng: Ok team — following up on the softcap failsafe idea I sketched yesterday. We need a concrete crossover behavior when a tenant exceeds softcap but we still have spare capacity.
kevin.m: +1 we should avoid hard cuts. Proposal: grant short-lived "grace credits" that let requests pass at slightly degraded priority for X seconds.
jia.li: How do we prevent grace credits from being gamed by bursty clients?
sarah.ng: Good Q. My thought: tie grace credits to a decaying token bucket per tenant plus a probe score. Credits only activate if probe_score < threshold (i.e., not abusive).
ryan_o: So probe_score is our existing abuse heuristic? We'll need to ensure latency-sensitive SLOs aren't impacted.
kevin.m: Right — implementation detail: when softcap triggers, router checks (1) probe_score, (2) tenant_recent_success_rate, (3) overall node utilization. If (1) passes and (3) < node_soft_limit, issue N grace credits with TTL 15s.
jia.li: We should also emit a telemetry event: `grace_credit_issued` with fields: tenant_id, credits, ttl, reason.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: rolling deploy queued for rate-controller v2 at 03:00 UTC :hourglass: 
sarah.ng: Nice. Also need to define observable behavior: clients should see 429 only after grace credits exhausted AND queue depth > Q. So transient spikes get absorbed.
ryan_o: Edge-case: what if many tenants get grace credits simultaneously? Could cause a second wave. We should cap total grace credits per node and have a global soft-failover knob.
kevin.m: Agreed. Cap per-node and per-cluster. Also add "crossover window" where we gradually demote priority instead of immediate evict. Sequence: full priority -> grace (best-effort) -> provisional (degraded rate) -> 429.
jia.li: For rollout, I'd prefer a flags-based approach. `rls.grace_enabled` + `rls.grace_max_per_node` + `rls.crossover_ttl`. Start conservative.
sarah.ng: Can someone sketch the router pseudocode? quick version is fine.
kevin.m: Sure —
```
if tenant.usage > softcap:
  if probe_score < abuse_threshold and node.grace_available > 0:
    issue_grace(tenant, n=3, ttl=15s)
  else:
    apply_provisional_admit(tenant)
```
jia.li: We'll need tests: synthetic burst from many tenants to ensure cap prevents second wave; abuse-simulation to verify probe_score blocks grace; and latency SLO test to ensure no tail regressions.
ryan_o: Also add a monitoring alert: `grace_credit_exhaustion_rate` > 5% for 5m -> paging. If grace credits are exhausted frequently, config is mis-tuned.
sarah.ng: Ops checklist before rollout: feature flag on, telemetry hooks in place, unit + integration tests, canary on 10% of nodes. I'll open a short RFC follow-up doc.
kevin.m: One more thought — tie grace credits to model-criticality tags. High-priority model calls (billing, auth) get lower chance of being throtled even out of grace.
jia.li: We'll need an interface contract: router needs `probe_score(tenant_id)` + `tenant_priority(tenant_id)` from admission API. Keep it simple: two ints.
sarah.ng: Perfect. Thanks all — I'll draft the RFC snippet and ping infra for canary window. :thumbsup:
